title: Which square tile side should Ziva pick for the room?
description: The factors of twelve and of sixteen are listed side by side, and the sizes on both lists are circled. The largest circled size is chosen because it covers the most floor. Keeko's doubt, a tile as long as the short wall, is tested on the plan and struck.
teaching_notes: One idea: a tile side must divide both walls, so it is a common factor, and the largest common factor needs the fewest tiles. Watch for students who choose the largest factor of one wall only.

source: Sameeksha's room is 12 ft by 16 ft. List the factors of 12 a
video_script.why: The child can list factors but has not yet used the factors of two numbers together to make a choice.
video_script.substitution: Every tile side that fits both walls is a number on both factor lists, so choosing the tile is choosing from the shared numbers.
video_script.anchor: The room of the book, twelve feet by sixteen feet, to be covered with square tiles of one size.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko picks the largest factor of the short wall, a twelve feet tile. It fills the short wall once but leaves a gap along the long wall, because sixteen is not a whole number of twelves.
video_script.payoff_line: Four feet is the best side.

final_answer.value: common factors 1, 2, 4; choose the 4 ft tile
final_answer.spoken: Ziva should choose the tile with side four feet

names.Ziva: builds a new house and tiles the main room (12 ft by 16 ft)

maths_rules: Room 12 ft by 16 ft; a square tile of side s fits a wall exactly when s divides the wall length.
Common factors of 12 and 16: 1, 2, 4. So tiles of side 1 ft, 2 ft or 4 ft fit both walls.
A larger tile covers more floor, so it needs fewer tiles; the largest common factor, 4, gives the fewest tiles.
Slip: a 12 ft tile fits the 12 ft wall once, but 16 = 12 + 4 leaves a 4 ft gap on the long wall; 12 is not a factor of 16.
video_script.design: One idea: the tile side must be on both factor lists, and the biggest shared one is best. Assumes the child can list factors. Wrong idea: Keeko picks the largest factor of the short wall. The plan stays all video; the two factor lists stay through the idea part.
